transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well. I guess I'm here because... I've been having a hard time shaking some things lately. I work as a financial advisor here in Cincinnati, and... I don't know, it's a little hard to explain. 

For a while now, I've just been... convinced that certain people—mostly in the arts and finance circles around here—are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. And... they keep sending me these little signals. Through things like event invitations, or specific panel topics... even just who ends up sitting near me at events. 

I keep trying to tell myself it could just be a coincidence, but... I can't really let it go. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
How long have you been noticing and feeling convinced about these signals and being tracked by people in the arts and finance circles?
Um... I'd say... it's been about two months. Yeah, around two months of... noticing all that.
Besides these signals you've noticed, have you also heard voices or sounds, or seen things that other people don't seem to hear or see?
No... I haven't. I don't hear voices or... see things that aren't there. It's really just... just what I already told you.
Over these past two months, have you also noticed any changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other hand, unusually energetic, elated, or needing much less sleep?
No... not really. I haven't noticed anything like that. My mood is... fine, I guess. I'm just sleeping the usual amount. It's really just the things I already mentioned.
Aside from these concerns about being tracked, has your ability to work, manage daily tasks, or interact with family and friends changed at all in the past two months?

I mean... I'm still working. But... I guess things have slowed down a bit. My practice is smaller right now. I just... I haven't been doing as many follow-ups. And I try to avoid going to public panels or networking events lately. It's just harder to keep up the same amount of contact with clients that I used to. But I'm still working.
Have you or people close to you noticed any changes in how you speak or organize your thoughts, or a decrease in your motivation, expressiveness, or interest in things you used to enjoy?

I don't know... maybe. I still get my work done, just... in pieces. I guess I just don't have the same spark right now. Like I said, I'll leave the client follow-ups sitting. 

And... I've been skipping things I usually do, like jazz nights or pickup basketball. I just don't really feel anything about missing them. When friends ask what's going on, I just give short answers. Talking just feels like... more effort than it should lately. But that's it, really.
Did you start noticing this drop in motivation and pulling back from friends around the same time you began feeling tracked, or did that actually start earlier?

It was... earlier. I guess it's been building for a while now. Probably... a little over two years ago. There was this recognition thing I got from an arts nonprofit, and... I don't know. It just sort of started changing after that.

Over these past two years, have people close to you commented that your facial expressions or emotional reactions seem flatter or less expressive than before, even when talking about things unrelated to being tracked?
No. Not really. I mean, nobody's said anything like that to me. I'm just... doing my thing.
When you skip things like jazz nights or basketball, is that mainly because you're trying to avoid being seen or tracked, or do you just not feel interested in them regardless of those concerns?
I don't know. I just... don't really want to go. It's not about being seen, I guess. I just don't care to.
Have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, or other recreational drugs or supplements over the past couple of years?
No. I don't really do any of that. Just... maybe a beer sometimes, but not really. I don't take anything.
